tagline: Over Deadman Summit to the salt shore of Mono Lake.
intro: US 395 comes into Mono County partway up the Sherwin Grade, tops Sherwin Summit and runs along the west shore of Crowley Lake. Then it leaves the Owens River behind and cuts across the Long Valley Caldera. Eight miles past the Mammoth turnoff it crests Deadman Summit at 8,036 feet, a pass named for a murder victim found nearby around 1868.

On the far side the road comes down to Mono Lake, squeezed between the water and the Sierra crest, then climbs to Conway Summit and over Devil's Gate Pass before following the West Walker River down toward Walker.

moments.title: Crowley Lake
moments.text: A reservoir for the Los Angeles Aqueduct since 1941, named for Father John Crowley, the desert padre who told the Owens Valley it could become a place for tourists.

moments.title: Mono Lake
moments.text: A lake with no outlet, about three times as salty as the ocean, where brine shrimp feed some two million migrating birds a year.

moments.title: Conway Summit
moments.text: At 8,138 feet the top of US 395, with the Sawtooth Ridge rising to the west and the Bodie Hills to the east.
